title: India Banks on Boxing, Athletics, and Weightlifting to Extend Top-Five Commonwealth Games Run
excerpt: With the 2026 CWG fast approaching, India's medal strategy hinges on its traditional strongholds while emerging sports like athletics could deliver breakthrough performances.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • India aims for a top-five finish at the 2026 Commonwealth Games, focusing on boxing, weightlifting, and wrestling.
  • Athletics, especially javelin and middle-distance running, could lead to significant breakthroughs for India.
  • Since 2010, India has consistently finished in the top five at the CWG, peaking with 66 medals in 2010.
  • Indian athletes compete in a diverse range of sports, broadening their medal opportunities compared to other nations.

India's campaign for the 2026 Commonwealth Games is taking shape around a familiar blueprint: dominate the combat and strength sports, compete hard in badminton and table tennis, and hope for breakthroughs in athletics and swimming that could push the medal tally into elite territory.

The Core Medal Sports

Boxing, weightlifting, and wrestling remain India's most reliable CWG medal factories. Indian boxers have consistently punched above their weight at the Games — pun intended — with the men's and women's squads expected to contribute multiple golds. Weightlifting has been equally productive, with lifters like Mirabai Chanu having established India as a genuine force in the sport.

Wrestling, traditionally strong at the CWG, where the field is thinner than at the Olympics or Asian Games, rounds out the combat sports trio. India typically harvests 15-20 medals from these three sports alone.

Athletics: A New Frontier
›Neeraj Chopra's javelin success inspires new athletes.
›Improved depth in shot put, discus, and middle-distance running.
›Potential for breakthrough performances in athletics.

The Athletics Question

The most exciting possibility for India's CWG campaign lies in athletics — a discipline where the country has historically underperformed at major events. That narrative has been shifting. Neeraj Chopra's javelin revolution has inspired a generation of field athletes, and India's depth in shot put, discus, and middle-distance running has improved markedly.

A breakout performance in athletics would not just add medals but fundamentally alter how India is perceived in the broader sporting world. Track and field success at a multi-sport event signals athletic depth in a way that combat sports alone cannot.

Beyond the Medal Count

For the Indian diaspora in CWG nations — the UK, Canada, Australia, and across the Caribbean — the Games carry a personal dimension that the Olympics do not. Many NRIs live alongside athletes from competing nations, creating neighborhood rivalries that extend from the living room to the stadium.

India has finished in the top five at every CWG since 2010, when the Delhi Games produced a record 66-medal haul on home soil. Maintaining that standard on foreign turf has been harder but achievable. The 2022 Birmingham Games saw India finish fourth with 61 medals.

The 2026 edition will test whether India's investment in Olympic-style sports is producing sustained competitiveness or whether the Delhi 2010 high-water mark was a host-nation anomaly. For a country that increasingly views sporting success as a matter of national prestige, the Commonwealth Games remain the broadest stage where India can compete credibly across the widest range of sports.
